$comment: This deployment's taskboard. DATA, not code -- and that is this file's whole argument.
The repository is a template, so the board's address is THIS deployment's value rather
than a property of the framework. A new deployment edits this file and does not touch
the skills.
UNSET SINCE 2026-09-10, AND THAT IS A STATE RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. The board this
file used to address belonged to the organisation this repository was forked out of.
It was emptied rather than renamed: the owner alone is not the address -- project_id
and every field and option id below belong to one specific board, and a renamed owner
over inherited ids points at a root where, as the paragraph below says, a null reads
exactly like an empty board. task-add and task-show refuse while `project_id` is empty,
which is the failure a person can act on. Fill this in from a board in this
organisation: `gh project list --owner <owner>` gives the number, and the REPAIR PATH
in .claude/skills/task-add/SKILL.md recovers the ids.
THE IDENTIFIERS ARE WRITTEN DOWN RATHER THAN DISCOVERED ON EVERY TASK. gh forces
that, not convenience: for a WORK ITEM (a draft item) there is no road by name. `gh
item-edit --field Status --value Backlog` refuses to work with `--id`, saying
'--field cannot be used with --id; use --url to address the item when editing by
name', and a draft has no URL, because it is not an issue. Only the form by id is
left: --project-id + --field-id + --single-select-option-id. Those ids do not appear
in the output of `gh project field-list` -- a single-select's option ids are in GraphQL
alone. That is why they stand here, and the query that recovers them is the REPAIR PATH
described in .claude/skills/task-add/SKILL.md. A discovery that was not written down is
a discovery the next session pays for a second time.
AN EMPTY 'options' IS INFORMATION, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Priority IS a single-select on
this board and has not one option defined. An empty map says so outright; a missing
entry would say only that somebody did not check.
owner_type picks the GraphQL query's ROOT: organization(login:) or user(login:).
gh project does not need it, GraphQL does -- and a null from the wrong root reads
exactly like an empty board.
Measured 2026-09-02 on gh 2.98.0.
